reasoning_summary: Baseline KNeighborsRegressor shows overfitting and high CV instability on a very small dataset, so the grid focuses on regularizing neighborhood behavior by varying neighborhood size, distance weighting, and distance metric choices while keeping the search compact.
search_strategy: Use a small-to-moderate n_neighbors sweep to reduce variance, compare uniform vs distance weighting, and test Minkowski with p=1/2 alongside explicit Euclidean and Manhattan metrics to capture both L1 and L2 behavior. Total combinations are 30.
expected_effect_on_overfitting: Increasing n_neighbors and using distance weighting may reduce sensitivity to individual training points and lower overfitting; metric choice may further stabilize local neighborhoods.
expected_effect_on_underfitting: Very large n_neighbors could increase bias and worsen underfitting, but the grid is capped at 10 to limit that risk on the small dataset.
computational_cost_estimate: Low to moderate: 30 total candidates, each inexpensive for n_train=21 and n_features=5.
warnings: For metric='euclidean' and metric='manhattan', p is ignored by sklearn but included here to keep the grid simple; some combinations may be redundant.
With only 21 training samples, CV estimates may remain noisy even after tuning.
KNN performance can be sensitive to feature scaling; ensure preprocessing is consistent.
